title: The imam's role
hookLine: the imam leads prayer and teaches, with no priesthood between a person and Allah

lines: A REST AREA, A JACKET ON THE GRASS.
FOR A FEW MINUTES, THE IMAM.
cards: Three friends on a road trip stop at a rest area when the time for prayer comes in. No mosque. No imam.
One of them lays a jacket on the grass to mark the direction. Then a small, friendly argument: you lead. No, you lead, you know more Qur'an.
Finally one steps a pace forward, the other two line up behind, and the prayer begins. For those few minutes, he's the imam. Then the prayer ends, and he's just the guy driving the next leg.

teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, Abu Mas'ud reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, saying, in paraphrase: the one who leads the people should be the one who best recites the Book of Allah, and if they're equal in that, the one who knows the Sunnah best.
That's the qualification. Not a family line, not an ordination. Recitation and knowledge.
So at a rest area, any qualified Muslim can lead.

At a mosque, the full-time imam usually leads the daily prayers, often gives the Friday sermon, teaches, marries couples, sits with grieving families and answers questions: a teacher, and a pastor of sorts in the everyday sense.
Now what the imam doesn't do.

teach.h: I AM NIGH: NO ONE IN BETWEEN.
teach.b: The Qur'an says, in Pickthall's translation: "And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me."
Allah answers the one who calls, directly. The imam stands in front so the rows can pray together. He doesn't carry their prayers for them, and no one needs him present to pray.

Another verse puts it closer still: "We are nearer to him than his jugular vein." Last, a word with more than one size. The Qur'an uses it for Ibrahim: "Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind."
The Arabic there is imam. And Shia Muslims use Imam, with a capital I, for the Imams of the Prophet's family, a role far larger than leading a prayer.

how: An imam leads the congregational prayer and, at a mosque, often preaches the Friday sermon, teaches and counsels; any qualified Muslim may lead a prayer, and individual prayer and supplication are made directly to Allah.

a priest who carries prayers up to God
leading the prayer and teaching, not mediating

games.q: three friends stop at a rest area for prayer. no mosque, no imam. who should lead, by the report in Sahih Muslim?
o: the one who best recites the Qur'an.
nobody; they should wait for a mosque.
games.why: the one who best recites the Book of Allah, then the one who knows the Sunnah best. any qualified Muslim can lead.

practice: Set aside any waiting for the right person, the right building or the right words, and bring to mind one thing on your heart today: a worry, a thank-you, a question.
If you pray, say it to Allah in your own words, silently, with no one in between; if not, put it into one plain sentence and let it sit there, unhurried.

wordCard.voice: The imam's role. To lead the prayer, teach and serve, chosen for recitation and knowledge, standing in front of the rows, not between a person and Allah. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a leader; the one who leads the prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: no one in between. The one in front leads the rows; the prayer is still yours. Go gently.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 673 (Abu Mas'ud: the one who best recites leads the people)
